trigger: a build-linux-coverage dir created before the fix
classification_rationale: the changelog fragment said the coverage build is configured with pkg_config_path, but the existing-dir --reconfigure branch never passed it, so a dir left by the #5803 link failure stayed broken
summary: Found independently by consistency-auditor, happy-path, security-guardian, build-ci and unhappy-path (all in the first parallel wave). The fix only reached fresh dirs; a reconfigure keeps a dir's cached options. Fixed by computing VCPKG_MESON_OPTS once and passing it to both paths, with a logged WARNING when the vcpkg tree or its pkgconfig dir is missing (UP-2/UP-3) and wording the warning as 'may fail to link'.

trigger: YUZU_COVERAGE_TIMEOUT_MULT set to 0 or a negative number (meson then disables every timeout, so a hung test hangs the gate with no outer bound) or to a non-number (meson runs zero tests)
classification_rationale: YUZU_COVERAGE_TIMEOUT_MULT was passed to meson unvalidated
summary: Reported by unhappy-path (UP-4/UP-5), security-guardian, build-ci and quality-engineer. Fixed by validating in tool_check() before any build, with a WARN gate row and the missing-tool exit semantics; the validation was tightened again in the second round (see g5803-multiplier-unbounded-and-sub1).

trigger: a reused build-linux-coverage dir and a run in which a previously passing test does not run to completion
line: coverage-gate.sh before the meson test run
classification_rationale: gcov counters accumulate across runs in a reused build dir, so a test that was skipped, killed or timed out keeps contributing its old counters and the figure cannot drop for lost tests
summary: UP-8 from unhappy-path; the reviewer capped it at MEDIUM citing E5/E7, but E5 does not lower a band and the artifact is not documented advisory in --full mode, so the derived band is HIGH (I3 base HIGH, no cap). Pre-existing, made likelier by the longer timeouts. Fixed by deleting *.gcda before meson test.

trigger: --build-dir that is a symlink resolving under an allowed prefix
classification_rationale: the first purge used find without -H, which does not follow a command-line symlink, so a symlinked --build-dir (accepted by the readlink -f path guard) kept its stale counters
summary: Found independently by happy-path (NICE), security-guardian (INFO) and unhappy-path UPR-1 (MEDIUM); the derived band is the same I3 class as g5803-stale-gcda-accumulates. A failed delete was also silent (UPR-4). Fixed with find -H, a logged WARNING when a delete fails, and CH-18 case C.

trigger: a gcovr whose help output exceeds 64 KB
classification_rationale: the probe `gcovr --help | grep -q` returns 141 under pipefail when the help exceeds the pipe buffer; and --branches is a text-report-only flag so probing for it was unnecessary
summary: Reproduced with a stub producer; real gcovr 8.6 help is 31 KB so it did not trigger. gcovr 8.6 JSON/XML/HTML are identical with and without the flag (build-ci, unhappy-path, happy-path). Fixed by removing the probe and the flag from the local gate.

classification_rationale: no test pinned pkg_config_path, the multiplier or the purge; the author's evidence was a probe run outside the script
summary: A missing test for a bounded blast radius is SHOULD at most; labelled SHOULD by the reviewer, derived LOW. Fixed by CH-18 (A fresh setup, B reconfigure + override + purge, C symlinked dir, D valid multipliers, E ten invalid multipliers asserted by the refusal note); every assertion was mutation-checked (6 mutations in round 1, 5 more in round 2). Remaining gaps recorded in g5803-harness-not-in-ci-and-gaps.

classification_rationale: comments and SKILL.md claimed the gate mirrors a ci.yml coverage job and Codecov; ci.yml has no coverage job and the only one is nightly.yml (gcc-15, linux-gcc15.ini)
summary: Corrected to nightly.yml with the gcc-13 vs gcc-15 native-file difference in the script and SKILL.md. SKILL.md also now says the native file applies when the build dir is created (consistency N1, pre-existing).

classification_rationale: the first regex accepted a 309+ digit string (meson crashes with OverflowError, zero tests run) and values under 1 (0.000001 kills every test)
summary: security-guardian and unhappy-path (UPR-2/UPR-8). Both outcomes are signalled (nonzero meson exit, partial note) so I8 rather than I3. Fixed: the regex now requires a number >= 1 with at most 6 digits each side.

trigger: a future validation regression; a scenario appended after CH-18
classification_rationale: the invalid-multiplier check would pass on any early WARN, no positive decimal was asserted, and CH-18 overwrote the shared $MOCKBIN mocks
summary: Fixed: refusal asserted through the gate row note, positive cases 1.5/12/1, private mock dir with PATH restored.

classification_rationale: the fragment was one dense bullet of about 150 words for contributor tooling
summary: enterprise-readiness and docs-writer. Tightened.

trigger: a non-Debian host whose pkg-config default path excludes system dirs
classification_rationale: setup.sh also appends the system multiarch pkgconfig dir and the caller's PKG_CONFIG_PATH; the gate passes the vcpkg dir only
summary: consistency-auditor, cross-platform, build-ci. cross-platform checked a Debian host: the default pkg-config search path already includes the system multiarch dir and libsystemd still resolved. No failing configuration was reproduced.

trigger: a deliberate bump of the gcovr pin (requirements-ci.txt, gcovr==8.6) to 8.7
classification_rationale: nightly.yml passes --branches to both gcovr calls and gcovr 8.7 removed the flag
summary: Verified for the flag: gcovr 8.6 help lists it as a deprecated text-report alias, 8.7 help does not. The workflow was deliberately not edited in this change (it cannot be exercised before it is on main). Tracked.

trigger: overlapping gate runs against the same worktree and --build-dir
classification_rationale: two gate runs on one build dir race and read each other's gcda; the new purge lets one zero the other's counters
summary: UP-14 from unhappy-path (MEDIUM). Independent adjudication by Codex Astra derived HIGH (E7 does not apply: SKILL.md documents enforcement in --full; E6 not established) and ruled fix-in-this-PR (a portable build-dir lock). Operator then directed a re-cut: tracked in #6112 for a follow-up PR.

trigger: a test killed on timeout (no gcda) or a failing meson test
line: coverage-gate.sh test run, metric writes and the line metric default
classification_rationale: failed or timed-out tests leave a lower figure that is recorded as an ordinary metric; the partial note goes on the gate row only; an unresolved line percent is written as 0.0
summary: UP-7/UP-13/UPR-3 from unhappy-path (MEDIUM). Codex Astra derived HIGH and ruled fix-in-this-PR; operator directed a re-cut, tracked in #6113.

trigger: disk full during the instrumented test run
classification_rationale: disk exhaustion truncates gcda while tests and gcovr exit 0; gate and metric DB writes are not checked
summary: UP-15 from unhappy-path (MEDIUM); Astra derived HIGH and ruled fix-in-this-PR; operator directed a re-cut, tracked in #6114.

trigger: a regression in the gate that no CI job would catch
classification_rationale: the PR2 harness is not run by CI, and CH-18 does not cover the refusal exit codes under --capture-baselines/enforce or the two missing-vcpkg warnings
summary: quality-engineer (F1/F2) and build-ci. Wiring it into CI changes Tier 1 runtime and exposes the older scenarios, so it is its own decision.

classification_rationale: a genuine hang in a 1500 s test is now detected after up to 4500 s
summary: UP-6 (unhappy-path), sre N2, happy-path F3. Accepted: wall-clock only, the operator can interrupt or lower YUZU_COVERAGE_TIMEOUT_MULT, and it is documented in the script header.

trigger: comparing a run at a different multiplier to the baseline
classification_rationale: the baseline does not record the multiplier it was captured under
summary: UP-9. A higher multiplier only lets more tests finish, which moves a measurement toward the truth; a baseline captured with truncated runs would be the lower one. Resolved from speculative to likely by reading the capture refusal (TEST_RC != 0) and the purge.

trigger: running tests/shell/test_pr2_gates.sh CH-18 on macOS, where /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp
classification_rationale: the scenario's fake root lived under a logical /tmp path; the gate's --build-dir guard resolves with readlink -f and compares to $YUZU_ROOT/build-*, so once the dir existed the guard refused it on macOS and 14 of the 15 assertions failed
summary: Found by actually running CH-18 on mini-colin (macOS 26.7.1, /bin/bash 3.2.57): no reviewer could run it on a Mac. The pre-existing guard is fail-safe (it refuses loudly) but also refuses a repo reached through a symlinked path on macOS; that guard was deliberately left unchanged.

reviewed_at_sha: the commit that follows 3537037da on fix/coverage-gate-local-hosts
summary: Fixed: the scenario now builds its fake root from `pwd -P`. Re-run on mini-colin under /bin/bash 3.2.57: CH-18 5/5 pass; the full harness passes 13 with 2 failures (CH-6, CH-15) that come from perf-gate.sh requiring bash 4+, which is not installed on that box and is untouched by this change.
